blocks.text: Bachon, pichhle do hisson mein humne hyperbola ki har khoobi alag alag dekhi. Ab un sab ko ek jagah, ek table mein jama karte hain, taa ke sawal hal karte waqt sab kuchh ek nazar mein saamne ho. Table ke do column hain: pehla us hyperbola ka jo baayen daayen khulti hai, doosra us ka jo upar neeche khulti hai. Phir hum dekhenge ke agar centre origin se hat kar kisi aur point \((h, k)\) par chala jaye to equation kaisi banti hai (Theorem 1 aur 2), aur aakhir mein chaar misaalen hal karenge. Is table ko ratne ki zaroorat nahi; agar aap ne 6.5.1 ki wajahen samajh li hain to har row khud ba khud yaad rahegi. Table ko bas ek naqshe ki tarah istemal kijiye jis se sawal hal karte waqt jaldi rasta mil jaye.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: \(\frac{y^2}{a^2} - \frac{x^2}{b^2} = 1\) wale sketch mein \(x\)-axis ke do points par \(B'(0, -b)\) aur \(B(0, b)\) likha hai. \(x\)-axis ke points par \(y = 0\) hota hai, is liye sahi labels \(B'(-b, 0)\) aur \(B(b, 0)\) hain, jaise table ki line 'Conjugate points \((\pm b, 0)\)' bhi kehti hai. Hamari drawing mein sahi labels hain.

Table ki har row ko pichhle section se jor kar dekhiye. Centre dono soorton mein origin hai. Transverse axis woh line hai jis par vertices aur foci hain; pehle column mein yeh \(x\)-axis ka tukra \(-a \le x \le a\) hai, doosre mein \(y\)-axis ka. Conjugate points \(B\), \(B'\) curve par nahi hote, sirf rectangle banane ke kaam aate hain. Eccentricity dono mein \(\frac{c}{a}\) hai aur hamesha 1 se bari. Latus rectum ki lambai dono mein \(\frac{2b^2}{a}\) hai, kyun ke shakal wahi hai, sirf 90 degree ghoom gayi hai. Sirf asymptotes ki slope badalti hai: pehle mein \(\pm\frac{b}{a}\), doosre mein \(\pm\frac{a}{b}\); is ki wajah yeh hai ke \(x\) aur \(y\) ki jagahen badal gayin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Table ko parhne ki kunji: POSITIVE term sab kuchh tay karta hai. Agar \(x^2\) positive hai to transverse axis, vertices, foci aur latera recta sab \(x\)-axis par hain aur directrices vertical lines \(x = \pm\frac{a}{e}\) hain. Agar \(y^2\) positive hai to yeh sab \(y\)-axis par chale jate hain aur directrices horizontal lines \(y = \pm\frac{a}{e}\) ban jati hain. Dono columns mein \(a^2\) positive term ka denominator hai aur \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\).
Sketch banane ki trick: \(A\), \(A'\), \(B\), \(B'\) se guzarta hua \(2a \times 2b\) ka dashed rectangle banaiye. Is ke diagonals ko lamba kar dein to woh asymptotes hain. Phir branches vertices se shuru kar ke asymptotes ke qareeb le jaiye.
Theorem 1: Translated Forms of Hyperbolas

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki heading mein "Hyperbola's" (apostrophe ke saath) chhapa hai. Sahi jama (plural) "Hyperbolas" hai: Translated Forms of Hyperbolas.
Equation

blocks.text_alt: x minus h squared over a squared minus y minus k squared over b squared equals 1

blocks.text: aisi hyperbola hai jis ke foci \(F'(h - c, k)\) aur \(F(h + c, k)\) par hain, jahan \(c = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\). Is ka centre \(C(h, k)\) par hai aur vertices \((h \pm a, k)\) par.
Is ki asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}(x - h) + k\) hain.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par cyan hyperbola baayen daayen khulti hui, centre C(h, k) laal horizontal axis par (daayen teer). Vertices A'(h - a, k), A(h + a, k); foci F'(h - c, k), F(h + c, k); kaali asymptotes y = (b/a)(x - h) + k aur y = -(b/a)(x - h) + k C par katti hain; laal khari directrices x = h - a^2/c aur x = h + a^2/c.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.25: Centre C(h, k) aur horizontal transverse axis wali translated hyperbola (kitab ki figure ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Theorem 1 asal mein wahi standard hyperbola hai, bas use utha kar is tarah rakh diya ke centre \((0, 0)\) se \((h, k)\) par aa jaye. Socho aap ne kaghaz par bani tasveer ko bina ghumaye khiska diya: shakal wahi rehti hai, sirf jagah badalti hai. Is liye har \(x\) ki jagah \(x - h\) aur har \(y\) ki jagah \(y - k\) aa jata hai. \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), \(e\) aur latus rectum wahi rehte hain.
Directrices \(x = \pm\frac{a}{e}\) ban jati hain \(x = h \pm \frac{a}{e}\), aur \(\frac{a}{e} = \frac{a}{c/a} = \frac{a^2}{c}\); isi liye Figure 6.25 mein \(x = h \pm \frac{a^2}{c}\) likha hai. Asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x\) ban jati hain \(y - k = \pm\frac{b}{a}(x - h)\), jo kitab wali \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}(x - h) + k\) hi hai.
Theorem 2
Equation

blocks.text_alt: y minus k squared over a squared minus x minus h squared over b squared equals 1

blocks.text: aisi hyperbola hai jis ke foci \(F'(h, k - c)\) aur \(F(h, k + c)\) par hain, jahan \(c = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\). Centre \((h, k)\) par hai aur vertices \((h, k \pm a)\) par. Is ki asymptotes \(x - h = \pm\frac{b}{a}(y - k)\) hain, yani \(y - k = \pm\frac{a}{b}(x - h)\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein Theorem 2 ki asymptotes \(x = \pm\frac{b}{a}(y - h) + k\) chhapi hain, jis mein \(h\) aur \(k\) ki jagahen ghalat hain. Sahi: \(x - h = \pm\frac{b}{a}(y - k)\), yani \(y - k = \pm\frac{a}{b}(x - h)\); Figure 6.26 mein bhi yahi likha hai. Khud check karne ka tareeqa: 1 ki jagah 0 rakhein to \(\frac{(y - k)^2}{a^2} = \frac{(x - h)^2}{b^2}\) milta hai.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par magenta X aur Y axes, origin O neeche baayen. Cyan hyperbola upar neeche khulti hui, centre C(h, k) magenta khari line par. Vertices A(h, k + a), A'(h, k - a); foci F(h, k + c), F'(h, k - c); kaali asymptotes y = (a/b)(x - h) + k aur y = -(a/b)(x - h) + k; magenta leti directrices y = k + a^2/c aur y = k - a^2/c.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.26: Centre C(h, k) aur vertical transverse axis wali translated hyperbola (kitab ki figure ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Figure 6.26 mein neeche wale vertex ka label \(A(h, k - a)\) chhapa hai; sahi \(A'(h, k - a)\) hai, kyun ke \(A(h, k + a)\) upar wala vertex hai. Hamari drawing mein sahi label hai.

Theorem 1 aur Theorem 2 ka muqabla kijiye. Dono mein centre \((h, k)\) hai aur dono mein \(c = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\). Farq sirf yeh hai ke Theorem 1 mein \((x - h)^2\) positive hai, to curve baayen daayen khulti hai aur vertices aur foci horizontal line \(y = k\) par hain, yani sirf un ka \(x\)-coordinate \(h\) se \(\pm a\) ya \(\pm c\) hilta hai. Theorem 2 mein \((y - k)^2\) positive hai, to curve upar neeche khulti hai aur vertices aur foci vertical line \(x = h\) par hain; ab \(y\)-coordinate \(k\) se \(\pm a\) ya \(\pm c\) hilta hai. Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: jo variable positive hai, usi ka coordinate hilta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Hyperbola \(\frac{(y + 1)^2}{16} - \frac{(x - 3)^2}{9} = 1\) ka centre, vertices aur foci kya hain? (Jawab: centre \((3, -1)\); \(y\) wala term positive hai to vertical; \(a = 4\), \(c = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5\); vertices \((3, 3)\) aur \((3, -5)\); foci \((3, 4)\) aur \((3, -6)\).)

Ab misaalen. Har misaal mein soch ka tareeqa ek hi hai: (1) centre kahan hai? (2) curve horizontal khulti hai ya vertical? (3) \(a\), \(c\) maloom karo, phir \(b^2 = c^2 - a^2\). Pehli misaal mein centre, axis ki lambai aur eccentricity di hui hai.

blocks.title: Example 23
blocks.problem: A hyperbola has a horizontal transverse axis of length 12, centre at \((-2, 5)\), and eccentricity \(\frac{5}{3}\). Find the equation of the hyperbola.
steps:
Diya gaya: horizontal transverse axis jis ki lambai 12 hai, centre \((-2, 5)\), eccentricity \(e = \frac{5}{3}\).
Maloom karna: hyperbola ki equation.
Tareeqa: transverse axis horizontal hai, to hyperbola baayen daayen khulti hai; is liye Theorem 1 wali shakal \(\frac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} - \frac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1\) lagegi. Humein chaar cheezein chahiye: \(h\), \(k\), \(a^2\), \(b^2\).

Standard form aur centre
\[\dfrac{(x - h)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(y - k)^2}{b^2} = 1\]
\[(h, k) = (-2, 5)\]
Kyun: curve horizontal khulti hai, is liye \(x\) wala term positive rakha. \((h, k)\) seedha diya hua centre hai.

\(a\) nikaalna
\[2a = 12 \Rightarrow a = 6\]
Kyun: transverse axis ki lambai hamesha \(2a\) hoti hai (ek vertex se doosre tak).

\(c\) nikaalna
\[e = \dfrac{c}{a} = \dfrac{5}{3}\]
\[\dfrac{c}{6} = \dfrac{5}{3} \Rightarrow c = 10\]
Kyun: eccentricity ki definition \(e = \frac{c}{a}\) hai; \(a = 6\) maloom hai, dono taraf 6 se multiply kiya.

\(b^2\) nikaalna
\[c^2 = a^2 + b^2\]
\[100 = 36 + b^2 \Rightarrow b^2 = 64\]
Kyun: hyperbola ka relation \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\) hai.
Dhyan dein: ellipse wala \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) yahan mat lagaiye, warna \(b^2\) negative aa jayega.

Values rakhna: \(h = -2\), \(k = 5\), \(a^2 = 36\), \(b^2 = 64\)
\[\dfrac{(x + 2)^2}{36} - \dfrac{(y - 5)^2}{64} = 1\]
Kyun: \(x - h = x - (-2) = x + 2\); minus minus plus ho jata hai.

Tasdeeq:
Transverse axis \(2\sqrt{36} = 12\), sahi. \(c = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\), to \(e = \frac{10}{6} = \frac{5}{3}\), sahi. Centre wahan hai jahan dono brackets zero hon: \(x = -2\), \(y = 5\), sahi. Saara diya hua data poora ho gaya.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar Example 23 mein transverse axis horizontal ke bajaye vertical hoti, baaqi sab wahi, to jawab kya hota? \(a = 6\), \(c = 10\), \(b^2 = 64\) wahi rehte, sirf shakal Theorem 2 wali ho jati: \(\frac{(y - 5)^2}{36} - \frac{(x + 2)^2}{64} = 1\). Dekhiye, sirf yeh tay karna ke kaun sa term positive ho, poora jawab badal deta hai; is liye sawal mein 'horizontal' ya 'vertical' ka lafz ghaur se parhiye.

Doosri misaal mein centre nahi diya, sirf foci aur axis ki lambai di gayi hai. Centre hum khud foci ke midpoint se nikalenge, aur foci ke coordinates dekh kar pehchanenge ke curve kis taraf khulti hai.

blocks.title: Example 24
blocks.problem: Find an equation of the hyperbola with given data and sketch the graph. (i) Foci: \((-3, 5 \pm 5\sqrt{2})\) (ii) Length of transverse axis \(= 6\).
steps:
Diya gaya: foci \((-3, 5 + 5\sqrt{2})\) aur \((-3, 5 - 5\sqrt{2})\); transverse axis ki lambai 6.
Maloom karna: hyperbola ki equation aur us ka sketch.
Tareeqa: centre foci ka midpoint hota hai. Dono foci ka \(x\)-coordinate ek hi hai, is liye transverse axis vertical hai aur Theorem 2 lagega. Phir axis ki lambai se \(a\), foci se \(c\), aur \(b^2 = c^2 - a^2\).

Centre
Foci ka midpoint centre hai:
\[C(-3, 5)\]
Kyun: centre dono foci ke bilkul beech hota hai. \(y\)-coordinates ka average: \(\frac{(5 + 5\sqrt{2}) + (5 - 5\sqrt{2})}{2} = \frac{10}{2} = 5\); \(\sqrt{2}\) wale hisse cancel ho gaye.

Equation ki shakal
Transverse axis vertical hai, is liye:
\[\dfrac{(y - k)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(x - h)^2}{b^2} = 1\]
Kyun: foci vertical line \(x = -3\) par hain, curve upar neeche khulegi, to \(y\) wala term positive aata hai.

\(a\) aur \(c\)
\[2a = 6 \Rightarrow a = 3\]
\[2c = \text{distance between foci} = 10\sqrt{2}\]
\[c = 5\sqrt{2} \Rightarrow c^2 = 50\]
Kyun: dono foci ke \(y\)-coordinates ka farq \((5 + 5\sqrt{2}) - (5 - 5\sqrt{2}) = 10\sqrt{2}\) hai, aur foci ke darmiyan faasla \(2c\) hota hai.
Dhyan dein: \((5\sqrt{2})^2 = 25 \times 2 = 50\), 10 nahi.

\(b^2\)
\[c^2 = a^2 + b^2\]
\[50 = 9 + b^2 \Rightarrow b^2 = 41\]
Kyun: hyperbola ka relation, \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\).

Matlooba equation
\[\dfrac{(y - 5)^2}{9} - \dfrac{(x + 3)^2}{41} = 1\]
Kyun: Theorem 2 mein \(h = -3\), \(k = 5\), \(a^2 = 9\), \(b^2 = 41\) rakha; \(x - (-3) = x + 3\).

Sketch (Figure 6.27)
Vertices \((h, k \pm a) = (-3, 8)\) aur \((-3, 2)\); foci \((-3, 5 \pm 5\sqrt{2})\), yani taqreeban \((-3, 12.07)\) aur \((-3, -2.07)\). Asymptotes:
\[y - 5 = \pm\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{41}}(x + 3)\]
Pehle centre \(C(-3, 5)\) se asymptotes khenchiye, phir ek branch \((-3, 8)\) se upar aur doosri \((-3, 2)\) se neeche banaiye, dono asymptotes ke qareeb jati hui.
Kyun: vertical hyperbola mein vertices centre se \(a\) upar aur \(a\) neeche hote hain, aur asymptotes ki slope \(\pm\frac{a}{b}\) hoti hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(c^2 = 9 + 41 = 50\), to \(c = 5\sqrt{2}\) aur foci \((-3, 5 \pm 5\sqrt{2})\), bilkul diye hue. Vertex \((-3, 8)\) rakhein: \(\frac{9}{9} - 0 = 1\), sahi. Transverse axis \(2 \cdot 3 = 6\), sahi.

blocks.alt: Example 24 ki exact graph, pale yellow panel par: magenta axes, dono par -20 aur 20 ke ticks. Cyan hyperbola (y - 5)^2/9 - (x + 3)^2/41 = 1 upar neeche khulti hai; centre C(-3, 5) magenta dot; vertices A(-3, 8), A'(-3, 2); foci F(-3, 5 + 5 root 2) upar aur F'(-3, 5 - 5 root 2) neeche. Asymptotes nahin bani.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.27: Example 24 ki hyperbola (kitab ki figure ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Figure 6.27 mein upar wale focus par \(F(-3, 5 - 5\sqrt{2})\) aur neeche wale par \(F'(-3, 5 + 5\sqrt{2})\) likha hai (dono labels ulte hain), aur neeche wale vertex par \(A'(-3, 8)\) likha hai. Sahi: upar wala focus \((-3, 5 + 5\sqrt{2})\), neeche wala \((-3, 5 - 5\sqrt{2})\), neeche wala vertex \(A'(-3, 2)\). Hamari drawing mein sahi labels hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 24 mein \(b^2 = 41\) aaya jo \(a^2 = 9\) se kahin bara hai. Is ka graph par kya asar hai? Asymptotes ki slope \(\frac{a}{b} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{41}} \approx 0.47\) hai, yani asymptotes kaafi 'leti hui' hain aur branches chauri ho kar phailti hain. Figure 6.27 mein yahi nazar aata hai.
Teesri misaal mein foci aur ek vertex diye hain. Yahan \(a\) aur \(c\) dono seedhe faaslon se mil jayenge, koi eccentricity nahi chahiye.

blocks.title: Example 25
blocks.problem: Find an equation of the hyperbola with given data and sketch the graph. (i) Foci \((4, -3)\), \((4, 7)\) and (ii) one vertex \((4, 5)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: foci \((4, -3)\), \((4, 7)\); ek vertex \((4, 5)\).
Maloom karna: hyperbola ki equation aur sketch.
Tareeqa: centre = foci ka midpoint; \(c\) = centre se focus ka faasla; \(a\) = centre se vertex ka faasla; phir \(b^2 = c^2 - a^2\).

Centre
\((h, k)\) foci \((4, -3)\) aur \((4, 7)\) ka midpoint hai:
\[h = \dfrac{4 + 4}{2} = 4, \quad k = \dfrac{-3 + 7}{2} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2\]
Yani centre \((4, 2)\).
Kyun: centre hamesha dono foci ke theek beech hota hai.

Transverse axis ki simt
Dono foci ka \(x\)-coordinate 4 hai, is liye transverse axis vertical hai aur shakal \(\frac{(y - k)^2}{a^2} - \frac{(x - h)^2}{b^2} = 1\) hogi.
Kyun: foci hamesha transverse axis par hote hain, aur yahan woh vertical line \(x = 4\) par hain.

\(c\) aur \(a\)
\[c = 7 - 2 = 5\]
\[a = 5 - 2 = 3\]
Kyun: \(c\) centre \((4, 2)\) se focus \((4, 7)\) tak ka faasla hai, aur \(a\) centre se vertex \((4, 5)\) tak ka. Dono ek hi vertical line par hain, is liye sirf \(y\) ka farq lena kaafi hai.

\(b^2\)
\[c^2 = a^2 + b^2\]
\[5^2 = 3^2 + b^2\]
\[b^2 = 25 - 9 = 16\]
Kyun: hyperbola ka relation.
Dhyan dein: \(b^2 = 16\), \(a^2 = 9\) se bara hai; hyperbola mein yeh bilkul theek hai.

Sketch (Figure 6.28)
Doosra vertex \((4, 2 - 3) = (4, -1)\) hai. Asymptotes:
\[y - 2 = \pm\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 4)\]
Ek branch \((4, 5)\) se upar khulti hai, doosri \((4, -1)\) se neeche.
Kyun: vertices centre se \(a = 3\) upar aur neeche hain; slopes \(\pm\frac{a}{b} = \pm\frac{3}{4}\).

Tasdeeq:
Vertex \((4, 5)\) rakhein: \(\frac{9}{9} - 0 = 1\), sahi. \(c = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5\), to foci \((4, 2 \pm 5)\), yani \((4, 7)\) aur \((4, -3)\), bilkul diye hue.

blocks.alt: Example 25 ki exact graph, pale yellow panel par: magenta axes, dono par -10 aur 10 ke ticks. Cyan hyperbola (y - 2)^2/9 - (x - 4)^2/16 = 1 upar neeche khulti hai; centre C(4, 2), vertices A(4, 5) aur A'(4, -1) kaale dots; foci F(4, 7) aur F'(4, -3) magenta dots aur magenta labels. Asymptotes nahin bani.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.28: Example 25 ki hyperbola (kitab ki figure ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Figure 6.28 mein neeche wale vertex par \(A'(4, 5)\) likha hai. Sahi \(A'(4, -1)\) hai (centre \((4, 2)\) se 3 unit neeche). Hamari drawing mein sahi label hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 25 mein sirf ek vertex \((4, 5)\) diya tha. Doosra vertex hum ne khud kaise nikala? Centre \((4, 2)\) dono vertices ke theek beech hota hai, to doosra vertex centre se utna hi neeche hoga jitna pehla upar hai: \(5 - 2 = 3\) upar, to doosra \(2 - 3 = -1\), yani \((4, -1)\). Yahi symmetry kitab ki figure ki ghalti pakarne mein bhi kaam aayi.

blocks.title: Numbering note (ours)
blocks.text: Kitab mein agli misaal par "Example 29" chhapa hai; Example 26 kitab mein kahin nahi, aur 29 ka number Section 6.6 ki pehli misaal par dobara aata hai. Hum ne is misaal ko us ki asal jagah ke mutabiq Example 26 likha hai (is se pehle Example 25 aur baad mein Example 27).

Chauthi misaal ulti simt se hai: yahan equation di hui hai aur humein us se saari khoobiyan nikaalni hain. Is ke liye completing the square ka purana tareeqa kaam aayega, jo aap ne circle aur ellipse mein bhi istemal kiya tha.

blocks.title: Example 26
blocks.problem: Find the centre, foci, eccentricity, vertices and equations of the directrices of the hyperbola: \(9x^2 - 36x - 4y^2 + 8y - 4 = 0\). Also sketch the graph.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(9x^2 - 36x - 4y^2 + 8y - 4 = 0\).
Maloom karna: centre, foci, eccentricity, vertices, directrices aur sketch.
Tareeqa: \(x\) aur \(y\) dono mein completing the square (mukammal murabba banana) kar ke equation ko translated standard form mein laana, phir \(h\), \(k\), \(a\), \(b\) parh lena.

Terms ko groups mein karna
\[9x^2 - 36x - 4y^2 + 8y - 4 = 0\]
\[9x^2 - 36x - 4y^2 + 8y = 4\]
\[9(x^2 - 4x) - 4(y^2 - 2y) = 4\]
Kyun: constant ko right par bheja, phir \(x^2\) aur \(y^2\) ke coefficients bahar nikale taa ke har bracket saada \(x^2\) ya \(y^2\) se shuru ho.
Dhyan dein: \(-4y^2 + 8y = -4(y^2 - 2y)\); bracket ke andar \(-2y\) aata hai, \(+2y\) nahi.

Murabba mukammal karna
\[9(x^2 - 4x + 4 - 4) - 4(y^2 - 2y + 1 - 1) = 4\]
\[9[(x - 2)^2 - 4] - 4[(y - 1)^2 - 1] = 4\]
\[9(x - 2)^2 - 36 - 4(y - 1)^2 + 4 = 4\]
\[9(x - 2)^2 - 4(y - 1)^2 = 36\]
Kyun: \(x\) ke coefficient \(-4\) ka aadha \(-2\), us ka square 4; \(y\) ke coefficient \(-2\) ka aadha \(-1\), us ka square 1. Jama aur tafreeq (add aur subtract) dono karne se value nahi badalti.
Dhyan dein: \(-4 \times (-1) = +4\) hota hai; yahan sign ki ghalti bahut aam hai.

36 se divide
\[\dfrac{9(x - 2)^2}{36} - \dfrac{4(y - 1)^2}{36} = 1\]
\[\dfrac{(x - 2)^2}{4} - \dfrac{(y - 1)^2}{9} = 1\]
Kyun: standard form mein right side par 1 hona chahiye. Yeh horizontal hyperbola hai: \(\frac{(x - h)^2}{a^2} - \frac{(y - k)^2}{b^2} = 1\).

Constants parhna
Yahan \(h = 2\), \(k = 1\), \(a^2 = 4 \Rightarrow a = 2\), \(b^2 = 9 \Rightarrow b = 3\).
\(c^2 = a^2 + b^2 = 4 + 9 = 13 \Rightarrow c = \sqrt{13}\).
Centre: \((h, k) = (2, 1)\).
Kyun: positive term \(x\) wala hai, is liye \(a^2 = 4\), chahe 9 bara number hai.

Vertices aur foci
Horizontal hyperbola ke vertices \((h \pm a, k)\): \(A(2 + 2, 1) = A(4, 1)\), \(A'(2 - 2, 1) = A'(0, 1)\).
Foci \((h \pm c, k)\): \(F(2 + \sqrt{13}, 1)\), \(F'(2 - \sqrt{13}, 1)\).
Kyun: vertices aur foci centre se guzarne wali horizontal line \(y = 1\) par hote hain.

Eccentricity aur directrices
\[e = \dfrac{c}{a} = \dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{2}\]
Horizontal hyperbola ki directrices \(x = h \pm \frac{a}{e}\):
\[\dfrac{a}{e} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}/2} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{13}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{13}}{13}\]
Yani directrices \(x = 2 \pm \frac{4\sqrt{13}}{13}\).
Kyun: directrices centre se \(\frac{a}{e}\) faasle par vertical lines hain; denominator se root hatane ke liye \(\sqrt{13}\) se upar neeche multiply kiya.

Sketch (Figure 6.29)
Asymptotes \(y - 1 = \pm\frac{3}{2}(x - 2)\). Ek branch \(A'(0, 1)\) se baayen, doosri \(A(4, 1)\) se daayen khulti hai.
Tasdeeq:
\(9(4)^2 - 36(4) - 4(1)^2 + 8(1) - 4 = 144 - 144 - 4 + 8 - 4 = 0\), yani vertex \((4, 1)\) asal curve par hai. \(e = \frac{\sqrt{13}}{2} \approx 1.80 > 1\), aur directrices \(x \approx 3.11\) aur \(0.89\) dono vertices ke beech hain, jaisa hona chahiye.

Cyan hyperbola (x - 2)^2/4 - (y - 1)^2/9 = 1 baayen daayen khulti hai; centre (2, 1) magenta dot; vertices A'(0, 1), A(4, 1); foci F'(2 - root 13, 1), F(2 + root 13, 1). Asymptotes nahin bani.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Figure 6.29 mein dono foci par \(F\) likha hai; baayen wala \((2 - \sqrt{13}, 1)\) \(F'\) hona chahiye. Aur \(x\)-axis par origin ke daayen tick par "0" chhapa hai, jo 10 hona chahiye. Hamari drawing mein sahi labels hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Hyperbola ka sketch banane ke paanch qadam, jo har sawal mein kaam aate hain:
1. Centre \((h, k)\) ka nuqta lagaiye.
2. Positive term dekh kar faisla kijiye ke curve baayen daayen khulegi ya upar neeche, aur centre se \(a\) faasle par dono vertices lagaiye.
3. Doosri simt mein centre se \(b\) faasle par conjugate points lagaiye aur \(2a \times 2b\) ka dashed rectangle banaiye.
4. Rectangle ke diagonals ko dono taraf lamba kijiye; yeh asymptotes hain.
5. Har vertex se branch shuru kijiye jo asymptotes ki taraf mude aur un ke qareeb tar hoti jaye, magar unhein kabhi na chhooye. Aakhir mein foci aur directrices ke nishaan laga dijiye.
Is tarah ka sketch exam mein do minute mein ban jata hai aur bilkul sahi shakal deta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 26 mein directrices \(x \approx 3.11\) aur \(x \approx 0.89\) aayin. Kya yeh sahi jagah par hain? Vertices \(x = 0\) aur \(x = 4\) par hain aur centre \(x = 2\) par. Hyperbola mein directrices hamesha centre aur vertices ke darmiyan, khali jagah mein hoti hain, kyun ke \(\frac{a}{e} < a\). \(0.89\) aur \(3.11\) dono 0 aur 4 ke beech hain, is liye jawab mantiqi taur par bhi theek hai. Aisi chhoti si soch se bahut si ghaltiyan pakri ja sakti hain.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Jab equation general form mein ho (jaise Example 26), to pehla qadam hamesha yeh dekhna hai ke \(x^2\) aur \(y^2\) ke coefficients ke signs ulte hain ya nahi. Ulte hon to hyperbola, ek jaise hon to ellipse ya circle. Phir completing the square kijiye aur aakhir mein right side ko 1 banaiye. Jawab mein centre, vertices, foci, \(e\) aur directrices alag alag lines mein, label ke saath likhiye; har cheez ke alag marks hote hain.

Ek nazar peeche: chaaron misaalon mein sawal alag alag shakal mein aaya, magar soch ek hi thi. Example 23 mein centre, axis ki lambai aur eccentricity di thi; \(e = \frac{c}{a}\) se \(c\) nikla. Example 24 aur 25 mein foci diye the; un ke midpoint se centre aur un ke faasle se \(c\) mila. Example 26 mein ulta kaam tha: general equation se completing the square kar ke standard form banaya aur phir sab kuchh parh liya. Har dafa teen sawal khud se poochiye: centre kahan hai, curve kis taraf khulti hai, aur \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) kya hain. In teen sawalon ke jawab mil gaye to baaqi sab sirf formula mein values rakhna hai. Aur aakhir mein tasdeeq zaroor kijiye: koi vertex ya diya hua point equation mein rakh kar dekhiye ke 1 aata hai ya nahi.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Pehle positive term dekhiye: wahi horizontal ya vertical batata hai, aur usi ka denominator \(a^2\) hai.
2. Theorem 1 \(\frac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} - \frac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1\): vertices \((h \pm a, k)\), foci \((h \pm c, k)\), directrices \(x = h \pm \frac{a}{e}\), asymptotes \(y - k = \pm\frac{b}{a}(x - h)\).
3. Theorem 2 \(\frac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} - \frac{(x-h)^2}{b^2} = 1\): vertices \((h, k \pm a)\), foci \((h, k \pm c)\), directrices \(y = k \pm \frac{a}{e}\), asymptotes \(y - k = \pm\frac{a}{b}(x - h)\).
4. Data se: centre = foci (ya vertices) ka midpoint; \(c\) = centre se focus; \(a\) = centre se vertex; \(b^2 = c^2 - a^2\).
5. General equation se: completing the square, phir divide kar ke right side 1.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Bare denominator ko \(a^2\) maan lena. Example 26 mein \(a^2 = 4\) hai, 9 nahi.
2. Negative coefficient ke saath murabba banate hue sign ki ghalti: \(-4(y^2 - 2y + 1 - 1)\) se \(+4\) aata hai, \(-4\) nahi.
3. Shift bhool jana: Example 26 ke foci \((2 \pm \sqrt{13}, 1)\) hain, \((\pm\sqrt{13}, 0)\) nahi.
4. Translated hyperbola ki directrices \(x = \pm\frac{a}{e}\) likh dena; sahi \(x = h \pm \frac{a}{e}\) hai.
5. \(b^2\) nikaalne ke liye ellipse wala \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) laga dena.
